summary: Officially retires the printed Assigned Numbers list from RFC 1700, which was a snapshot of protocol parameters from October 1994. Those values are now kept in an online database. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: This memo retires RFC 1700, a printed list of assigned Internet numbers. It points readers to the online database that had replaced the periodically published list.

questions: where did rfc 1700 assigned numbers go
what replaced the assigned numbers rfc
subtitle: The memo that retires the printed Assigned Numbers RFC in favor of an online database.

tldr.problem: RFC 1700 contained a dated snapshot of Internet protocol parameter assignments, and its values were incomplete and sometimes wrong.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 3232 records that the Assigned Numbers series had been replaced by an online database and formally obsoletes RFC 1700.
tldr.outcome: RFC 1700 changes to Historic status. RFC 3232 is Informational and says the series might be revived in the future.

today: RFC 3232 is Informational and has no later obsoleting or updating RFC listed in the unit metadata. It obsoletes RFC 1700, which it moves to Historic status.

sections.title: The Assigned Numbers Series
sections.content:
From November 1977 through October 1994, the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA) periodically published tables of Internet protocol parameter assignments in RFCs titled Assigned Numbers. The latest document in that series was RFC 1700, which had Standard status and the designation STD 2.

RFC 1700 contained an October 1994 snapshot of the assignments. This memo explains that the series had since been replaced by an online database.
sections.plainLanguage: IANA used to publish lists of Internet number assignments in RFCs. RFC 1700 was a snapshot from October 1994.

sections.title: RFC 1700 Becomes Historic
sections.content:
RFC 3232 officially obsoletes RFC 1700 and changes its status to Historic. It warns that RFC 1700 is obsolete, its values are incomplete, and some values may be wrong. The online database had replaced the printed list.

The memo says the authors expect the series to be revived by the new IANA organization in the future. It does not specify a protocol or new parameter values.
sections.plainLanguage: The old list is no longer a reliable source for current assignments. The memo directs readers to the online database and says the list series could return later.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC states that the memo does not affect the technical security of the Internet. Its purpose is to record the change from a periodically published list to an online database.
sections.plainLanguage: This memo changes where people look up assigned values. It does not change Internet security.

references.text: Reynolds, J. and J. Postel, "Assigned Numbers", STD 2, RFC 1700, October 1994.
